issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or stalls when slowing down or stopping, and may be hard to restart.
issues.why: Stalling while driving is the top engine complaint for these years. Owners and mechanics point to a misadjusted or failing throttle position sensor, idle problems, or fuel delivery faults.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the throttle position sensor, idle setting and fuel pressure checked. Stalling in traffic is dangerous, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Misfires and stumbling from worn ignition parts
issues.sym: Misfires, stuttering on acceleration, rough running, stalling or a no-start, sometimes worse in rain.
issues.why: These small engines are sensitive to worn spark plugs and plug wires. Moisture in the distributor cap or wires can also cause misfires.
issues.next: Replace plugs, wires, cap and rotor with parts made for this engine. It is a simple first step for most running problems.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start from failed distributor pickup
issues.sym: The engine turns over normally but won't start, or it fires briefly and then loses spark.
issues.why: The pickup or module inside the distributor can fail and stop the spark. Owners report cranking with no start at high mileage.
issues.next: Have a shop check for spark while cranking. If spark is missing, the distributor or its pickup is a common fix.

issues.t: Rough idle from leaking throttle body gasket
issues.sym: Uneven or high idle, or stumbling when you press the gas.
issues.why: The throttle body gasket can leak air, letting unmeasured air into the engine.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke-test for vacuum leaks. Replacing the gasket is a simple fix.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt loosens or breaks
issues.sym: A wobble or knock from the front of the engine, belts squealing or coming off, loss of power, or the engine shutting off.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) can back out or break. A loose pulley can wear through the timing belt cover and damage the timing belt.
issues.next: If you hear a new knock or see the pulley wobble, stop driving and have it checked. Fixing it early avoids timing belt and engine damage.

issues.sym: A whirring or chirping from the timing belt area at the front of the engine.
issues.why: The timing belt tensioner pulley bearing wears. The belt and tensioner are usually replaced together.
issues.next: Have the timing belt and tensioner inspected and replace them if worn or due. Follow the mileage interval in the owner's manual.

issues.sym: Coolant loss, overheating, white exhaust smoke, or an oil level that rises because coolant is getting into it.
issues.why: A failing head gasket lets coolant leak into the oil or cylinders. Overheating makes it more likely.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats or the oil looks milky. A head gasket job usually includes resurfacing the head and a new timing belt.

issues.t: Engine clatters until warm on the 1.0L
issues.sym: A rattling or clattering from the engine on cold starts that quiets down once warm.
issues.why: Owners describe this as normal wear on the three-cylinder engine, most often from worn pistons and bearings.
issues.next: Check the oil level and use the correct oil. If the noise stays when warm or gets louder, have it checked.

issues.t: Drive belt squeals on cold mornings
issues.sym: A squeal from the engine at startup in cold weather, worse with the lights, heater and radio on.
issues.why: The alternator and water pump belt slips when it is loose or glazed.
issues.next: Tighten the belt to spec or replace it. Don't over-tighten it, which can wear out the water pump bearing.

issues.sym: Clicking when turning, a torn rubber boot with grease thrown around the wheel, or vibration when accelerating.
issues.why: Front axle failures are among the most reported Metro problems, often around 95,000 miles. A torn boot lets dirt into the joint.
issues.next: Have the CV boots checked at oil changes. Replacing a boot early can prevent an axle replacement.

issues.sym: A bouncy, floaty ride at highway speeds, nose-diving when braking, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: RepairPal lists worn front struts, around 75,000 miles, as the most common Metro problem.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts inspected. Replace them in pairs and get an alignment.

issues.t: Check engine light from loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A gas cap that doesn't seal sets an evaporative emissions code.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few drives, replace the cap and have the codes read.

issues.sym: The engine revs but the car doesn't speed up, especially going uphill, or the car hesitates and jerks between shifts.
issues.why: The clutch cable needs adjustment as the clutch wears. Once the adjustment is used up, the clutch disc is worn out.
issues.next: Have the clutch pedal free play adjusted. If there is no adjustment left, the clutch needs replacing.

issues.t: Loses power with a full tank on automatics
issues.sym: The car feels sluggish or idles high, mainly right after filling the tank.
issues.why: A blocked vent hose between the fuel tank and the charcoal canister can keep the tank from venting properly.
issues.next: Have the tank vent hose and charcoal canister checked for blockage.

issues.t: Water pump leaks at high mileage
issues.sym: Coolant drips near the front of the engine, the coolant level drops, or the engine runs hot.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears and starts to leak at high mileage. It sits behind the timing belt.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. Replace the water pump when the timing belt is done to save labor.

issues.t: Headlights go out while other lights work
issues.sym: The headlights stop working while the taillights or other lights still work.
issues.why: A loose or corroded ground wire from the light assemblies or between the battery and body is a common cause.
issues.next: Have the ground wires and connectors cleaned and tightened before replacing switches or bulbs.

issues.t: Driver seat back can collapse in a rear crash
issues.sym: The seat back gives way or the seat rocks. In some reported rear-end crashes the seat collapsed backward.
issues.why: Owners report broken seat brackets and seat backs folding back in rear impacts.
issues.next: If the seat feels loose or rocks, have the seat frame, brackets and recliner inspected and repaired.

issues.t: Shift lever can slip out of Park (recall)
issues.sym: The automatic shift lever looks like it is in Park but can be moved without the key or button, and the car may roll on a slope.
issues.why: A defect in the automatic shift lever let it come out of Park on uneven ground. GM recalled about 33,000 1997 Metros.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: ABS light on with stored trouble codes
issues.sym: The ABS warning light comes on and the anti-lock brakes may not work. Normal braking still works.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the ABS light coming on with codes 46 and 86 on Metros with ABS.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read and ask the shop to check the GM bulletin.
